merger_description:
Apiam Animal Health Pty Ltd (**Apiam**) proposes to acquire the remaining 50% of the issued share capital of South West Equine Veterinary Group Pty Ltd (**SWE**), an equine veterinary clinic located in Warrnambool, Victoria (the **Acquisition**). As a result of the Proposed Acquisition, Apiam’s interest in SWE will increase from 50% to 100%.

SWE is an equine veterinary clinic located in Warrnambool at the Warrnambool Racing Club. It provides full ambulatory and in-clinic equine veterinary services. The clinic is a partnership between the Ballarat Veterinary Practice and Warrnambool Veterinary (Apiam) and is controlled by Apiam together with BVP Holdings Pty Ltd (**BVP Holdings**).

BVP Holdings is selling its 50% interest in Southwest Equine Veterinary Group on behalf of Ballarat Veterinary Practice.

Apiam is a rural veterinary business, comprising more than 80 veterinary clinics and ancillary business sites across Australia, and supplies a range of veterinary services across Australia, including companion animal, equine, dairy, beef cattle, sheep and goat, pig, poultry and mixed animal veterinary services, together with veterinary diagnostics, emergency and after-hours services. Apiam is ultimately owned and controlled by funds managed and advised by Adamantem Capital Management.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. Apiam already holds a 50% share in SWE and currently
manages and is responsible for the day-to-day operations of
the clinic, and the Acquisition does not create any new
horizontal overlap between Apiam and SWE in the supply of
equine veterinary services in the south-west region of
Victoria
b. there are alternative providers supply of equine veterinary
services in the south-west region of Victoria.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
